pages.note: The upper three quarters of the page — nineteen printed lines, single column, justified run-on prose. It completes the Aṭṭhamī offering that began on page 68: the first words on this page, สะพ์รัห์มะเก, close the unit page 68 cut in half, so verse 9 is COMPLETED rather than added and stays on page 68 where its line starts. The passage then runs to สุขายะ. and STOPS — no colophon, no จบ line. Three superscript footnote markers sit in it: 1 and 2 on verse 39, 3 on verse 51, and all three footnotes are printed under a rule at the foot of this page. One word is broken across a line break with a hyphen, สัมมา- / สัมพุทโธ on verse 13, and is rejoined.

Below the offering, under its own centred title, which the book sets on TWO printed lines — สะระภัญญะคาถา above and สำหรับสวดในวันอัฏฐมีบูชา below. No chant number. SET IN TWO COLUMNS: one printed line runs across both, the left cell holding the first pāda and the right the second, read across the row. Only TWO rows are printed before the page runs out at the footnote rule, so the chant does not end here and page 70 carries the rest.

Under a rule at the foot of the page: three numbered footnotes in Arabic numerals, keyed to the superscripts in the offering passage above. All three are EDITORIAL notes telling the chanter which word to use, not canonical citations, so no source_printed is written for this page. They are word for word the three notes page 67 prints under the identical passage, and are entered identically.

checks.issue: THIS VERSE COMPLETES THE LINE PAGE 68 CUT. Page 68 ended mid-unit at สะเทวะเก โลเก สะมาระเก and recorded it with […]. Page 69 opens with สะพ์รัห์มะเก, which closes the unit, so the whole line as printed across the two pages is สะเทวะเก โลเก สะมาระเก สะพ์รัห์มะเก, — entered against verse 9, NOT as a new verse, and carrying NO page key because it STAYS ON PAGE 68, which is where the line starts. Same handling as the p51/p52 completion already in the file.

สะพ์รัห์มะเก here and สัสสะมะณะพ์ราห์มะณิยา on verse 10 both carry the small mark over พ and over ห, read on an isolated 4x crop of line 1. Entered with U+0E4C (์) like everything on pages 51 to 68. This is the same open question about WHICH mark this printer cuts that pages 51 to 60 raised, not a new one.

A WORD REJOINED ACROSS A LINE BREAK. The justified passage breaks mid-word: line 2 ends อะระหัง สัมมา- with a hyphen and line 3 opens สัมพุทโธ,. The hyphen is typesetting, not spelling, so the word is rejoined as สัมมาสัมพุทโธ and the hyphen dropped, matching the twin's verse 14 on page 66.

POINTED DIFFERENTLY FROM ITS TWIN. This page prints โลกะวิทู. with a FULL STOP; page 66's Visākha twin prints โลกะวิทู, with a comma at its verse 17. Read at 3x on an isolated crop — the mark sits on the baseline with no tail. Reproduced as printed, so this chant has a sentence break where the twin runs on. One look settles which the printer intended.

อัชะลีกะระณีโย, as printed, where standard editions have อัญชะลีกะระณีโย (añjalikaraṇīyo). Read at 3x: there is no ญ, the word is อั-ชะ-ลี. The app already holds the same reading from page 67 verse 38, so the book agrees with itself across both printings. Kept as printed and transliterated to match — Ajalikaraṇīyo, not Añjalikaraṇīyo.

TWO FOOTNOTE MARKERS SIT IN THIS VERSE — a superscript 1 on ถูโป and a superscript 2 on กะโต. Both keyed notes are EDITORIAL, telling the chanter which word to use, not canonical citations, so no source_printed is written and the markers are not carried into the chanted text. Page 67 carries the identical two markers on the identical verse and was handled the same way. The notes themselves go in as page blocks.

THE AṬṬHAMĪ CHANT NAMES THE VISĀKHA FULL MOON. This page prints อิมัง วิสาขะปุณณะมีกาลัง, exactly as page 66's Visākha twin does, read at 3x on an isolated crop. It is not an error to correct: Aṭṭhamī falls on the eighth day reckoned FROM the Visākha full moon, so the season is named the same way, and what differs is the next unit — สะรีรัชฌาปะนะกาละ, the time of the cremation of the body, where the twin has ชาติสัมโพธินิพพานะกาละ, birth, awakening and final nibbāna. Reproduced as printed, but worth one look because it reads as a mistake if you do not know why it is there.

ONE UNIT HERE WHERE THE TWIN HAS TWO. Page 69 prints สะรีรัชฌาปะนะกาละสัมมะตัง ปัต์วา อิมัง ฐานัง สัมปัตตา, with NO comma after ปัต์วา — checked at 3x, the gap between ปัต์วา and อิมัง is clear white with no mark. Page 66's twin prints ชาติสัมโพธินิพพานะกาละสัมมะตัง ปัต์วา, and then อิมัง ฐานัง สัมปัตตา, as two units. Entered as this page prints it, so the two chants divide the same sentence differently.

TWO UNITS HERE WHERE THE TWIN HAS ONE. This page prints ยะถาภุจเจ คุเณ, with a comma and then อะนุสสะรันตา, on the next line; page 67's twin runs them together as ยะถาภุจเจ คุเณ อะนุสสะรันตา, at its verse 51. The comma after คุเณ was read at 3x at the right-hand end of line 15. The English is split across the two units to match, which is why verse 50 reads only 'recollecting them,'.
A THIRD FOOTNOTE MARKER, superscript 3 on ถูปัง, keyed to the third editorial note at the foot of the page. Same handling as markers 1 and 2 on verse 39, and the same as page 67 verse 52.

THREE UNITS HERE WHERE THE TWIN HAS TWO. This page prints สุจิระปะรินิพพุโตปิ, / ญาตัพเพหิ, / คุเณหิ อะตีตารัมมะณะตายะ ปัญญายะมาโน, — commas after สุจิระปะรินิพพุโตปิ and after ญาตัพเพหิ, and NONE after คุเณหิ, all read at 3x on isolated crops of lines 17 and 18. Page 67's twin has สุจิระปะรินิพพุโตปิ ญาตัพเพหิ คุเณหิ, then อะตีตารัมมะณะตายะ ปัญญายะมาโน, — so the two printings break the same sentence in different places, and this one separates ญาตัพเพหิ from the คุเณหิ it agrees with. Reproduced as printed. The English is redistributed across the three units and keeps the twin's wording.

PRINTED WITHOUT THE SMALL MARK. This page prints ปะฏิคคัณหาตุ with nothing over the ณ, read at 3x on an isolated crop; page 67 prints ปะฏิคคัณ์หาตุ WITH the mark at its verse 59, and the app holds it that way. Page 68 found the same omission on the same word. So the word appears three times in three pages, marked once and bare twice. That is the book being inconsistent about whether the mark is there AT ALL, which is a different question from which of the two marks it is. Each kept as its own page prints it.

THE CHANT ENDS HERE, at สุขายะ. with a full stop, and there is NO colophon — no จบ line, no closing formula. Below it the page goes straight to the next chant's centred title after a gap of about one line, and that white holds no ink. So the closing key is left off rather than composed, exactly as it was for the Visākha twin, which also ends bare on page 67.

NOT AN ERROR ON THIS PAGE, BUT WORTH ONE LOOK IN THE FILE. The Visākha twin already in chanting.py has 'Sucirapaṇinibbutopi' as the pali_roman of its verse 56, where its own pali reads สุจิระปะรินิพพุโตปิ — parinibbutopi, with r. It looks like a transliteration slip in existing data rather than anything the book did. Nothing was changed; this page's verse 55 is transliterated Suciraparinibbutopi from what is printed here.

checks.issue: SET IN TWO COLUMNS, AND THIS IS THE FIRST PAIRING, which is the reading that has to be confirmed. One printed line runs ACROSS both columns: the left cell holds วิสาขะปุณณะมายัชชะ and the right cell ทิวะโส โหติ อัฏฐะโม, joined into the single verse วิสาขะปุณณะมายัชชะ ทิวะโส โหติ อัฏฐะโม. Reading down the left column alone gives วิสาขะปุณณะมายัชชะ / ยาทิเส นะระเทวัสสะ, which is two unfinished half-lines rather than continuous Pali, so the rows read across. Same setting as the Saraphañña verses for Visākha on pages 67 and 68.

NO PUNCTUATION AT THE END OF THIS ROW. อัฏฐะโม is printed bare, with the full stop falling on row 2 after ตาทิโน. — the same couplet pointing the Visākha Saraphañña uses, where the stops fall on the even rows. Read at 3x on an isolated crop of the right cell; the paper after อัฏฐะโม is clear.

THE ENGLISH OF THIS COUPLET IS A WORKING TRANSLATION AND NEEDS YOUR EYE. yādise is a locative agreeing with an unexpressed 'day', so the couplet says something like 'today is the eighth day, such a day as was that of the god among men, the Such-one, come to his final quenching'. The page prints no Thai translation to check it against, hence english_unverified. sunibbutassa could carry either the general sense of full quenching or the specific one of the pyre being quenched, which is what Aṭṭhamī commemorates; the plainer reading was written rather than the pointed one.

THE CHANT DOES NOT END ON THIS PAGE. Only two rows of it are printed, and beneath them is the footnote rule and the three notes — so the page simply runs out. It is listed in batch_status.continues and carries continues: true. Page 70 has not been read, so how many more rows there are is not known; the Visākha Saraphañña that opens the same way on page 67 ran to thirty. If page 70 turns out to start something else instead, the CONTINUES marker comes off then.
NO CHANT NUMBER. The book prints no number before this title, exactly as it printed none before the Visākha Saraphañña on page 67, so book_number is left off rather than counted.
